articles.title: Never After Dark review – ghostbuster-for-hire meets her match in Japanese exorcism horror
articles.summary: Shogun’s Moeka Hoshi stars as a travelling caster-out of ghosts who confronts a wounded and recalcitrant spirit in this inventive chiller. If you watched this Japanese-language ghost-story horror thriller cold, you might be a little surprised that the credits reveal that the director is one Dave…
body: More recently, Boyle was a key director-producer for the Netflix series House of Ninjas, and Never After Dark seems to have evolved as a spun-off side hustle between Boyle and Ninjas star Kento Kaku, who produced it and takes a supporting role.
That all goes a little way to explain how this ends up feeling like a larky, low-stakes, one-for-funsies exercise – inventive and full of charm even if the scares are sort-of predictable.

Shogun ’s Moeka Hoshi stars as Airi, a young woman who looks like a hipster with her torn jeans and raggedy haircut and who travels the country in her Volvo as an itinerant ghostbuster for hire. The ghost of Airi’s dead older sister Miku (Kurumi Inagaki) is always by her side but is only visible in mirrors (as per folklore), and is available to give advice about imminent danger and vibes in the spirit world.

articles.title: Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE’s Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers
articles.summary: The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers.
body: The partnership comes as SIFF increasingly looks beyond screenings and workshops to the practical hurdles facing young filmmakers trying to enter the industry. Ahead of the festival, SIFF director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety that learning to make a film represents only one part of that journey.

“Our agreement with the National Media Authority reflects this commitment,” Al Qasimi said Monday. “It is an important step in bringing together national efforts to support the film industry and help emerging filmmakers turn their ideas and perspectives into creative work.”

The new agreement addresses another piece of that infrastructure. The National Media Authority will help facilitate permits required to screen participating films, coordinating, where necessary, with embassies, consulates, cultural organizations and government entities. Festival teams will also receive training on the authority’s electronic services and technical support intended to streamline regulatory procedures.
points: Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers.

articles.title: Instagram Is Testing Ability to Share Videos up to 90 Minutes Long and Launches on Apple TV — but Unlike YouTube, It’s Still Not Going to Pay Creators
articles.summary: Meta’s Instagram is trying to make itself a better place for watching and sharing longer-form entertainment content from digital creators, including testing out video lengths of up to 90 minutes and letting users watch Reels and more on Apple TV.
body: Instagram announced the test of the new features in (of course) a video shared Monday on the platform.

“Instagram is all about connecting people over creativity. And creativity is so much more than just short-form video or posting carousels,” Instagram VP of product Tessa Lyons said in the video, alongside Instagram head Adam Mosseri. Lyons said Instagram wants to accommodate creators who are telling stories in different ways on the platform, such as in episodic series, and that it’s seeing some sharing clips from long-form videos to drive discovery of that content.

Mosseri noted, “I have been against doing long-form video on the platform for a long time.” One of his concerns historically has been “how do we make sure that we keep Instagram not just about entertainment, but also about connecting with friends.”

“If you watch a video [on Instagram] for 10 or 20 or 30 minutes, it’s a lot of Reels, photos and carousels that you might not have sent to a friend,” which means fewer likes and shares, he said. But now, Mosseri has been sold on the need for Instagram to “lean into” long-form videos, including on TVs.

articles.title: Bad Day at the Office review – gratuitously entertaining Go-Pro thriller is like Crank meets The Hangover
articles.summary: John Hannah parkours through gangland London in a hyperactive first-person action film that has to keep the heartrate down. This ludicrous, rabid thriller, shot largely on first-person GoPros, is like Peep Show on PCP.
body: Hannah plays Karl Davis – or that is apparently his name, when this amnesiac wakes up to a Hangover-like bombsite of a hotel room. He’s got a banging headache, party detritus is littered everywhere, and there is a dead body in the bathtub. Or perhaps this scenario is Crank inverted; Davis has left a box of pills and a note to self to take one whenever his heart rate gets too elevated. Which of course happens 10 seconds later. A pair of fake police officers arrive to search the room, only for Davis to trounce them with scary efficiency, just as maid Molly (Radha Mitchell), with whom he shacked up the night before, walks through the door.

articles.title: Walter Koenig, Chekov on Original ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90
articles.summary: Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Variety has confirmed. He was 90.
body: “Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft.

“Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen. Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.
“On behalf of all of us, we extend our deepest condolences to Walter’s family, friends, colleagues, and the millions of fans whose lives he touched over the decades.
“Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”
points: Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Variety has confirmed.
“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit.

articles.title: Harry Styles Waltzes His Way Through ‘Coming Up Roses’ Music Video
articles.summary: Harry Styles puts his waltzing skills to the test in the video for “Coming Up Roses,” the latest single to get the music video treatment from his fourth album “Kiss All the Time.
body: Styles initially hinted at the release of the music video during the 27th of 30 shows at New York City’s Madison Square Garden on Saturday night. The singer is currently on his “Together, Together” tour, which will conclude its MSG residency on October 31. He’ll wrap up this leg of the trek in Melbourne and Sydney in November and December before picking back up in Glendale, Arizona in April.

Following his Arizona shows, Styles will perform a series of shows in respective cities including Arlington, Pasadena, Toronto, Chicago, Berlin, Nanterre, Madrid, Rome and Dublin. He’ll bring this live era to a close with three shows at London’s Wembley Stadium on August 24, 27 and 28.

Variety recently broke the news that famed documentary director John Wilson has been rolling cameras on Styles at MSG since August, capturing footage for a doc expected to blend live performances with a glimpse into Styles’ world. One source described it as featuring authentic human stories of everyone involved in the tour, from the singer and his fans to the countless others behind the scenes.

body: But when the group decide to protest at Elbit Systems, the Israeli-owned arms manufacturer, its actions slide into “criminal mischief and criminal trespassing”, according to reports. articles.title: ‘Vicarious wish-fulfillment’: why That Thing You Do! is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our ongoing series of writers explaining their most rewatched comfort films is a journey back to the 90s for Tom Hanks’ heartfelt 60s-set music comedy. “How did we get here?” That’s the question Steve Zahn’s character in That Thing You Do!
body: It’s a moment I have thought of many times over the past 30 years. Sometimes, it’s been a moment I’ve aspired to, and sometimes it’s a moment I’ve felt myself. When the band hears their song on the radio for the first time, it’s one of the most ebullient moments I’ve ever seen on film. There is a euphoria that is recognizable for anyone who has ever felt the joy of a creative accomplishment – and isn’t that all of us, in one way or another? That’s what makes That Thing You Do! my feelgood movie.

In 1996, Tom Hanks was on top of Hollywood. He had back-to-back best actor Oscar wins, and two of 1995’s highest-grossing films with Toy Story and Apollo 13. I presume he could have done anything he wanted. I will be forever grateful that he chose to write, direct and co-star in this modest, gentle ode to 1960s pop music. It’s a movie of such warmth that any scene viewed at any time will instantly make me happier.

articles.title: Russell Brand asked assistant for female fan phone numbers, court hears
articles.summary: Helen Berger said she left her job working for Brand after she became "sick of him."
body: A former personal assistant of Russell Brand has told a court she was instructed to get phone numbers for the entertainer from female fans when she first started working with him.

Helen Berger, who worked closely with Brand from June 2006 to February 2007, said the request "felt uncomfortable" and, after seeking advice, she told the TV personality that she would not do that anymore.
Brand, 51, is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one charge of indecent assault.
The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.

articles.title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
articles.summary: The R&B star previously pleaded guilty to affray, after attacking a music producer with a glass bottle.
body: US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.
The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.

Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 costs.
Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown's use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head "was plainly dangerous", adding that the violence of the attack was "intense".

articles.title: ‘Minimum Wage’ Review: Netflix’s Format-Breaking Hangout Series Makes Good on the Promise of Short Episode Running Times
articles.summary: 'Fresh Off the Boat' star Randall Park is the biggest name in this adaptation of the web series of the same name from production company American High.
body: There were plenty of reasons why Quibi, the short-form streaming platform, failed within eight months of its 2020 launch.

I made fun of Quibi and I’ll continue to, but one thing I won’t deny: The executives behind Quibi were probably right that shorter episodes were a key element of the future of storytelling, if not the entirety of the future.

Two weeks ago, Freeform released Coven Academy, a supernatural YA drama that aired on television with standard episodic lengths but then streamed with episodes running between 12 and 23 minutes. I won’t tell you that Coven Academy is a good show, but thanks to the length of episodes it moves along like gangbusters, especially at a time when power players like HBO and Netflix still insist that hour-long dramas should be closer to 65 or 70 minutes per episode if they’re “prestigious.”
Enter Minimum Wage, a streaming version of the web series of the same name from the production company American High.
